title: A precheck test fails when the machine is busy
what: The test proves the registry message is not hidden by a slow changed test without depending on wall-clock speed: a fake clock or an injected budget, never a real 3 s limit. Then max(20, ceil(3/p)) clean runs under load prove it.
why: 28 Oct: tests/test_precheck.py::test_a_slow_changed_test_does_not_hide_the_registry_message (landed 28 Oct 10:06 in cae100fb) gives the registry-only test group a 3 s wall-clock budget. With several gates and agents running, that group timed out and turned the queue-time branch's gate red (the probe's library tests took 906 s). The test passed 3 of 3 runs alone at about 4 s each. Neither the test nor lib/relay_precheck.py was in that branch's diff.
failing_case: Run tests/test_precheck.py while 2 gates and 4 agents run: test_a_slow_changed_test_does_not_hide_the_registry_message times out on the 3 s group budget.
pass_cases: 20 clean runs of the test with `stress`-like CPU load (e.g. 6 busy python loops).
With the registry-first order removed, the test still fails (it guards the fix, not the clock).
